'''Gas Transmission Northwest''' is an operating natural gas pipeline in Canada and the United States.<ref name=tc>[http://tcplus.com/GTN About Gas Transmission Northwest LLC], TransCanada, accessed January 2018</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs from Kingsgate, British Columbia, to Malin, Oregon.

==Background==
Gas Transmission Northwest (GTN) is a 1,353 mile-long natural gas pipeline built in 1961 with a capacity of 2,900 million cubic feet per day.<ref name=tc/> It brings gas from Alberta, Canada, beginning at Kingsgate, British Columbia and passing through Washington and terminates at Malin, Oregon then connecting to California, connecting to the Pacific Gas and Electric system.<ref name=tc/>

Prior to being purchased in 2004 by TC Energy (formerly known as TransCanada Corporation), the pipeline was named Pacific Gas Transmission.<ref name=Wiki>[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas_Transmission_Northwest Gas Transmission Northwest], Wikipedia, accessed January 2018</ref> TC Energy subsequently sold 25 percent of its interest in GTN to TC PipeLines, LP, which connects via the Tuscarora Gas Pipeline.<ref name=Wiki>[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas_Transmission_Northwest Gas Transmission Northwest], Wikipedia, accessed January 2018</ref> GTN's FERC code is 86.<ref name=Wiki>[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas_Transmission_Northwest Gas Transmission Northwest], Wikipedia, accessed January 2018</ref>

==Expansion Projects==
===GTN XPress===
In November 2019 TC Energy proposed expanding the pipeline's capacity by 250 million cubic feet per day, with a completion date of 2023.<ref name=Globe>[https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2019/11/01/1939332/0/en/TC-PipeLines-LP-announces-GTN-XPress-to-enhance-market-access-for-growing-WCSB-supply-and-allow-additional-market-penetration-along-GTN-s-system.html TC PipeLines LP announces GTN XPress to enhance market access for growing WCSB supply and allow additional market penetration along GTN’s system], Globe Newswire, Nov. 1, 2019</ref> The project will increase imports into Canada via Kingsgate, Idaho, USA.<ref name=eia1021>[https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php Natural Gas, Pipeline Projects], Energy Information Administration, accessed July 12, 2021</ref>

As of mid-2022, the developers had applied to FERC for approval.<ref name="eia1021" /> The application asks FERC's permission to retrofit the existing pipeline to increase its capacity to "serve the growing market demand its system is experiencing." This would include an upgrade to four compressor stations located in Idaho, Washington, and Oregon. These upgrades would increase pressure and transport more gas through the system.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pstrust.org/why-the-gtn-xpress-expansion-project-isnt-safe/|title=https://pstrust.org/why-the-gtn-xpress-expansion-project-isnt-safe/|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://federalregister.gov/documents/2022/11/25/2022-25715/gas-transmission-northwest-llc-notice-of-availability-of-the-final-environmental-impact-statement|title=Federal Register :: Request Access|website=federalregister.gov|language=en|access-date=2023-08-17}}</ref>

On 26 July 2023, Oregon Senators Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden sent a letter to FERC following up on previous requests to reject approval for this expansion project.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wyden.senate.gov/news/press-releases/merkley-wyden-urge-ferc-to-reject-fossil-gas-pipeline-expansion|title=https://www.wyden.senate.gov/news/press-releases/merkley-wyden-urge-ferc-to-reject-fossil-gas-pipeline-expansion|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> Climate activists allege that the expansion would result in 3.47 million metric tons of greenhouse gas emissions annually and generate a social cost of around $12 billion.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://missoulacurrent.com/gas-pipeline-northwest/|title=US energy regulator greenlights gas pipeline expansion across Northwest|work=The Missoula Current News - Daily News in Missoula Montana|access-date=2023-08-17|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.doj.state.or.us/media-home/news-media-releases/western-state-attorneys-general-seek-to-halt-capacity-expansion-of-gtn-pipeline/|title=Western State Attorneys General Seek to Halt Capacity Expansion of GTN Pipeline - Oregon Department of Justice|last=Ally Nguyen|date=2022-08-22|work=Oregon Department of Justice|access-date=2023-08-17|language=en-US}}</ref> The project would lock the northwest into depending on expensive fossil fuel energy for decades. The expansion is inconsistent with Washington's and Oregon's targets to reduce emissions by 95% and 80%, respectively, by 2050.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rogueclimate.org/our-work/gtn/|title=Stop GTN Xpress|last=|first=|date=|website=Rogue Climate|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=17 August, 2023}}</ref>

In October 2023, FERC approved the project. Construction commenced in July 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://us-east-1.storage.xata.sh/m70jvtbk0kiboe951dh79h8oebcon23k|title=GTN Express In Service Request|date=2024-11-13|website=Oil & Gas Watch|url-status=live|access-date=2025-06-01}}</ref> It was successfully completed by the end of 2024.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.tcenergy.com/operations/natural-gas/gas-transmission-northwest/|title=TC Energy — Gas Transmission Northwest|website=www.tcenergy.com|access-date=2025-06-02}}</ref>

*'''Parent company:''' TC Energy<ref name=":1" />

*'''Status: '''Operating<ref name="eia1021" />

==Opposition==
In July 2023, opponents of GTN Xpress – including the governors of Washington, Oregon, and California – accused TC Energy and other utilities involved for using faulty projections of rising demand to justify the GTN Xpress project. The attorneys general of all three states have formally asked FERC to reject the proposal. TC Energy would avoid extensive environmental permitting processes by upgrading compressor stations along the 60 year old GTN pipeline than building a new one.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.desmog.com/2023/07/20/tcenergy-gtn-pipeline-expansion-northwest-climate-change/|title=Proposed Pipeline Expansion Could Upend Three States' Climate Plans|last=Nick Cunningham|date=2023-07-20|work=DeSmog|access-date=2023-09-08|language=en-US}}</ref>

In a draft environmental impact statement released by FERC in June 2022, the completion of the GTN Xpress would enable addition of 3.24 million metric tons of CO2 per year to the atmosphere. This number was lowered to 1.9 million metric tons in the final environmental impact statement released five months later. FERC excluded the impact of Tormaline's portion of the project, stating that since the Tourmaline is a Canadian producer and it’s not clear who they will sell the gas to, the emissions “are not reasonably foreseeable."<ref name=":0" />

Opponents of the proposed project feared that FERC would approve the project in all likelihood.<ref name=":0" />

In October 2023, FERC approved the expansion project with bipartisan support.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tcenergy.com/newsroom/statements/tc-energy-appreciates-fercs-bipartisan-approval-of-its-gtn-xpress-project/|title=TC Energy Appreciates FERC’s bipartisan approval of its GTN XPress Project|website=www.tcenergy.com|access-date=2025-06-02}}</ref>
